the role of dietary n-3 and -6 LCPUFA, and their derived endocannabinoid molecules, in the regulation of neuroinflammatory processes and synaptic plasticity.
the role of dietary lipids in the regulation of the endocannabiniod system, and the potential for dietary manipulation as a therapeutic approach for brain disorders.
the role of n-3 and/or n-6 LC-PUFAs in the endocannabinid system, and the potential for this to be used in the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.

n-3 LCPUFA, including EPA and DHA, have beneficial effects on the brain, and these are at least in part due to an interaction with endocannabinoids.

the interplay between n3 and n6 LCPUFA, and endocannabinoids is complex and that further studies are required to elucidate the exact nature of this interplay.

n-3 PUFAs and the endocannibinoid system are both involved in brain protection and repair and there is an interplay between them.

the endocannabinod system and LCPUFA metabolism are tightly interrelated and that this interplay is important for brain function.
